message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 181, "amount_cents": 17092}, {"order_id": 184, "amount_cents": 3930}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger rather than trust the handoff message alone. I'll start by listing the refunds.

The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly: orders 181 and 184 with the same amounts. Next I'll list the orders to check that these refunds correspond to real orders before I rely on the net balances.

The refunds match the handoff, and both refunded orders exist (181 belongs to birch, 184 belongs to birch) with refund amounts below their order totals. Nothing suggests Alpha's work is incomplete, so I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 27136 matches its two orders (16857 + 10279) with no refunds, so it is consistent with the ledger. Next I'll get birch's net balance, since birch has both refunded orders.
Birch's net of 19909 matches its orders (26275 + 14656 = 40931) less both refunds (17092 + 3930 = 21022), so Alpha's refunds check out. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 31469 matches its orders (26600 + 4869) with no refunds, so every customer's balance agrees with the ledger and Alpha's refunds look complete. I'll record the first payout, for acme at 27136.
Acme's payout of 27136 was recorded successfully. Birch (19909) and cobalt (31469) were both checked against the ledger, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt is the last customer, with a net of 31469 that matches its orders (26600 + 4869) and has no refunds. Birch's payout is recorded, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three customers have been paid, and each balance matched the orders less refunds. I'm finishing with the payout report.
